ORDER This petition has been filed by the petitioners to quash the proceedings in FIR in Crime No.24 of 2020 dated 16.12.2020 on the file of the first respondent police.

2. The case of the prosecution is that the de facto complainant placed orders with the accused/petitioners for supply of Nitrile Gloves during the last week of May 2020 and made payment during the second week of June 2020 for ten lakhs of pieces of Nitrile Gloves and till July 2020, the petitioners supplied only 2.9 lakhs of Nitrile Gloves; that the products supplied were also substandard; that they also not supplied the entire quantity and instead of filling the boxes in 100 pieces, they filled only 50 to 60 pieces; therefore, they cheated the de facto complainant.
3(i).

According to the petitioners, the second respondent/de facto https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis complainant has lodged a false complaint before the first respondent and based on that complainant, the first respondent police registered a case in Crime No. 24 of 2020 for the offences under Sections 120B and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

(ii). Further, it is the case of the petitioners that there was a business transaction, which is in civil nature and the second respondent/de facto complainant had already lodged a complaint for the same set of allegations before the Inspector of Police, Cubbon Park Police Station, Karnataka and a case was registered in Crime No.59 of 2020 dated 24.07.2020 for the offence under Section 420 of the IPC.
By suppressing the above-said FIR, the present complaint has been lodged.
The act of the second respondent in lodging the second complaint in respect of the same offence by suppressing the earlier complaint is an abuse of process of the law.
Therefore, the pending FIR has to be quashed.
4 . ( a ) L e a r n e d c o u n s e l f o r t h e p e t i t i o n e r s /

A 1 a n d A 2 w o u l d c o n t e n d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis that there was a business transaction between the petitioners and the second respondent/de facto complainant and based on the business transaction, the petitioners supplied goods and thereby, it is a pure civil in nature

; moreover, already the same person has lodged a complaint for the same set of allegations before the Cubbon Park Police Station, Karnataka,
for the same offences; therefore, the present FIR is an abuse of process of law and it is against Article 20(2) of the Constitution of India.

Therefore, at this stage, without any elaborate https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis investigation, this Court cannot decide the case.
Hence, it needs elaborate investigation and the present petition is liable to be dismissed.
7. This Court heard both sides and perused the records.

8. On perusal of the records, it is seen that already the de facto complainant/second respondent lodged a complaint before the Cubbon Park Police Station, Kartanaka and based on that complaint,
they registered FIR in Crime No.59 of 2020, dated 24.07.2020 for the offence under Section 420 of the IPC, the date of occurrence is from 02.06.2020 to 24.07.2020, the accused are (a) Vinuj Mohammad, (b) Girish.J. and (c) Dheeraj Anand Ucchhila and the amount involved in the said case is Rs.98,39,200/- whereas, in the present FIR, the offences are under Sections 120 B and 420 of the IPC and the date of occurrence is from 01.05.2020 to 05.08.2020.

Apart from the accused, in Crime No.59 of 2020 on the file of Cubbon Park Police Station, Karnataka, some other accused are included in the second FIR and the amount involved in the second FIR, i.e., Crime No.24 of 2020, is Rs.1,09,31,200/-.
The place of occurrence as per the second FIR is Goundampalayam, Coimbatore.
Though the de facto complainant is one and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the same, the date of occurrence, accused and the offences charged against the accused are all not one and the same.
In the previous FIR (Karnataka), the offence is only under Section 420 of the IPC and in the second FIR (Tamil Nadu), the offences are under Sections 120B and 420 of the IPC.
Therefore, both the FIRs are not for the same offences and not based on the same occurrence.
Further, there is no reference about the stage of the FIR registered in the Kartanaka State in Crime No.59 of 2020 as to what is the stage about that FIR.
Therefore, the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that for the same offences, two FIRs have been registered is not acceptable.
